name: Harvard PhD Program in Neuroscience (PiN)
summary: Full-time, lab-based neuroscience PhD with a core curriculum, drawing on more than 150 faculty at hospitals and campuses across the Boston area. First-year students rotate through labs before starting dissertation research.

deadlines.label: Application deadline
deadlines.note: PiN's apply page says December 1 at 5:00pm EST, without a year; its timeline lists a January 2027 interview weekend. The Griffin GSAS program page lists Dec 01, 2026, 5:00 pm.

timeline.interviews: Interview invitations go out in late December. The interview weekend is January 21–23, 2027 in Boston; each applicant has five faculty interviews and one student interview.
timeline.decisions: GSAS sends offers in mid-February, waitlist offers follow in March and April, and admitted students must decide by April 15.

english.toefl: 5 overall, Speaking 4.5 (tests from 21 Jan 2026); 100 overall, Speaking 23 (earlier tests)
english.note: IELTS Speaking minimum 6.5. Required if English isn't your native language and your undergraduate degree wasn't taught in English. PiN accepts no other proof, a graduate degree does not count, and the rule applies whatever your citizenship. For Fall 2027, tests must be taken no earlier than January 5, 2025.

applicationFee.note: Waiver eligibility is worked out by questions in the Application Fee section of the application. The fee is not refundable.

requirements.note: The statement of purpose is limited to 1000 words and the personal statement to 500. Only students who enroll send official transcripts (due in July). A committee of PiN faculty reads every section in a holistic review, and letters from research advisors are the most informative.

funding.note: All PiN students, regardless of citizenship status, get full tuition support, a monthly stipend, health coverage and a relocation allowance while enrolled and making satisfactory progress. The 2025–26 total is $51,500 over 12 months: a $50,460 stipend plus a $1,040 dental and transportation subsidy. GSAS lists six years of funding for Neuroscience.

international.note: All applicants are reviewed in the same pool with no demographic quotas. PiN says about 30% of its current students are international.
